project.name: nuv
project.description: A CLI tool that scaffolds opinionated uv-based Python projects from archetypes, producing a ready-to-run project with click, logging, tests, and linting all passing from the first commit.

nodes.name: _validate_python_version

nodes.name: cli
nodes.summary: Top-level Click group callback that configures logging from the --log-level option and shows help (exiting non-zero) when invoked without a subcommand.

nodes.name: new_cmd
nodes.summary: Click command implementing nuv new: collects name, archetype, python-version, install-mode, and keep-on-failure options and delegates project creation to run_new, mapping errors to exit codes.

nodes.name: main

nodes.name: validate_name

nodes.name: render_template

nodes.name: generate_jupyter_notebook
nodes.summary: Builds a valid Jupyter notebook JSON document with markdown and code cells seeded for the generated project, parameterized by name and python version.

nodes.name: scaffold_files
nodes.summary: Writes the shared baseline project files (python-version, gitignore, logging, main, pyproject, README, tests) then dispatches to the archetype-specific scaffolder for spark, fastapi, or polars.

nodes.name: _scaffold_spark
nodes.summary: Generates the spark archetype layout, writing the src package, config and session modules, jobs package, tests, and an explore notebook.

nodes.name: _scaffold_fastapi
nodes.summary: Generates the fastapi archetype layout, writing the application package, routes, an app factory, a multi-stage Dockerfile, and httpx-based tests.

nodes.name: _scaffold_polars
nodes.summary: Generates the polars archetype layout, writing the package modules, an explore notebook, and the data/raw and data/features directories for the local data lake.

nodes.name: run_uv_sync
nodes.summary: Runs uv sync in the generated project, raising RuntimeError when uv is not installed or the subprocess exits non-zero.

nodes.name: run_tool_install
nodes.summary: Optionally installs the freshly scaffolded project as a tool, validating the install mode and invoking uv, with logging and RuntimeError on failure.

nodes.name: resolve_target
nodes.summary: Resolves the target directory for a new project from the name and optional --at path, raising when the destination already exists.

nodes.name: run_new
nodes.summary: Top-level orchestrator for nuv new: resolves defaults and target, validates the name, scaffolds files, runs uv sync and tool install, and removes the directory on failure unless keep_on_failure is set.

tour.title: What nuv Is and Why
tour.description: Start with the README to understand nuv's purpose: `nuv new my-tool` scaffolds an opinionated uv-based Python project that is fully working — click CLI, logging, tests, and linting all green from commit zero. The pain it solves is the gap left by `uv init`, which only produces a stub; nuv closes the distance between an empty project and writing real code. This document also introduces the four archetypes (script, spark, fastapi, polars) that the rest of the tour will trace through actual code.

tour.title: The CLI Entry Point
tour.description: The console script `nuv = nuv.cli:main` lands here. cli.py uses Click to define the `nuv` command group and the `nuv new` command, declaring every option from the README (--at, --archetype, --python-version, --install, --keep-on-failure) and validating them before any work happens. It configures logging via the small _logging helper, then delegates the actual scaffolding to commands/new.py — keeping the command surface thin and the orchestration separate.
tour.languageLesson: Click builds CLIs declaratively: @click.group() defines a parent command and @click.command() with @click.option() decorators turn function parameters into validated flags. Choice types (e.g. click.Choice) reject invalid archetype names at parse time, so the engine never sees bad input.

tour.title: The Scaffolding Engine
tour.description: This is the heart of nuv and the most depended-upon module in the codebase. commands/new.py runs the full orchestration that backs `nuv new`: validate inputs, resolve the target directory, render shared templates, generate a Jupyter notebook, dispatch to the archetype-specific writer (script/spark/fastapi/polars), run `uv sync`, optionally install the tool, and clean up the directory on any failure. Building on the thin Click layer from Step 2, this is where the README's promise of a ready-to-run project is actually fulfilled.
tour.languageLesson: The cleanup-on-failure pattern wraps the scaffold steps so a partially-written project directory is removed if anything raises — unless --keep-on-failure is passed. In Python this is typically a try/except that shutil.rmtree's the target on error, guaranteeing no half-built projects are left behind.

tour.title: How Archetypes Are Located
tour.description: Archetype templates live as directories under src/nuv/templates/. At scaffold time, the engine from Step 3 resolves templates from its filesystem templates root and then joins the selected archetype name and template filename to find the correct .tpl payloads. The __init__.py files in templates/ and its archetype subdirectories identify those folders in the source tree, but the current template lookup described here is path-based rather than package-resource-based.
tour.languageLesson: Python's pathlib makes simple filesystem-based resource lookup explicit: code can compute a templates root relative to __file__ and then append path components such as the archetype name and template filename. That approach differs from package-resource APIs like importlib.resources, so docs should describe the path join the code actually performs.

tour.title: Designing a New Archetype
tour.description: The polars archetype is a useful case study because its template files are excluded .tpl payloads not surfaced as code nodes — the design lives in these documents instead. The spec details the Polars + DuckDB + Delta structure, modules, dependencies, and template wiring, while the plan breaks the work into six concrete tasks spanning CLI registration, templates, the scaffold function, and tests. Together they show the exact recipe a contributor follows to extend the engine from Step 3 with a new archetype.

tour.title: Why a Scaffolder Needs Heavy Tests
tour.description: A tool whose entire value proposition is "everything passes from commit zero" must prove it, and this 100+ test pytest suite does exactly that. test_new.py exercises both the Click layer from Step 2 and the engine from Step 3: option validation, template rendering, notebook generation, uv sync and tool-install behavior, and full end-to-end scaffolding for all four archetypes. Because generated projects are themselves checked for passing tests and clean linting, the suite guards the core guarantee against every change.
tour.languageLesson: pytest favors plain functions with fixtures over class hierarchies. The tmp_path fixture gives each test an isolated temporary directory — ideal for a scaffolder, since every test can generate a real project on disk and assert on the result without polluting the repo or colliding with other tests.

tour.title: Build & Project Configuration
tour.description: pyproject.toml is the single manifest tying everything together: it declares the click dependency, registers the `nuv = nuv.cli:main` console entry point that makes Step 2 reachable as a command, and configures pytest, ruff, coverage, and the hatch build backend. The .python-version pin fixes the interpreter for developing nuv itself, and the justfile collects the lint/test workflows into convenient task-runner recipes so contributors run the same checks locally that CI runs remotely.
tour.languageLesson: In pyproject.toml, [project.scripts] maps a command name to a module:function target (here nuv -> nuv.cli:main). When the package is installed, the build backend generates an executable shim on PATH that imports and calls that function — this is how a Python library becomes a runnable CLI.

tour.title: Enforcing Green From Commit Zero
tour.description: CI/CD is the capstone that turns nuv's promise into an enforced invariant. The ci.yml workflow lints, type-checks, and runs the full pytest suite from Step 6 on every push and pull request, so a regression in the scaffolding engine can never merge silently. The publish-pypi.yml workflow builds the distribution defined by pyproject.toml from Step 7 and publishes it to PyPI on tagged releases, completing the path from source to the installable tool described in the README.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use `on` triggers (push, pull_request, or tag patterns) to decide when to run, and `jobs` made of sequential `steps`. Gating release on a tag pattern while gating tests on every push is a common split: validate continuously, publish deliberately.
